summary: Recorded the decisive receipt for the RestoreCommittedLogs configuration question. Receipt f4adc58c4125434eb91cacf438a6da50 parsed all six events and evaluated all seven comparisons: the feature-on construction contradicts the assertion that the node uses the committed configuration entry in its own log (witness index 3: latest index 1, membership {A,B,C}, quorum 2, lastApplied 7), the live node contradicts it through the public GetConfiguration (witness index 5: {A,B,C}), the feature-off control on identical stores holds (index 1: latest index 6, {A,B,C,D,E}, quorum 3, lastApplied 5), and the mechanism operands hold in both modes (index 3 at 7, index 1 at 5). The experiment-level interpretation is violated/asserted with those exact indices; the question-level account is now explained/asserted, keeping the supplied-fixture, unexecuted-election, unobserved-persistence and store-coverage limits, retaining the earlier receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e as a channel failure that supports nothing. I also registered the follow-on question of whether a stale-configured node can actually win an election with fewer votes than a majority of the configuration in its own committed log while the remaining voters elect their own leader. Not filed this turn: the partition/election witness experiment, whose harness (bootstrap {A,B,C}, snapshot on A, add D and E through real AddVoter calls, restart A with RestoreCommittedLogs, then split A and C from B,D,E and sample leader counts in both partitions against a no-restore control) still needs local construction before execution.
